I’ve been farming these 7.8 mu for 30 years. I only finished primary school, but I know this land better than any book. This year I’ll keep 6.5 mu in wheat-maize rotation and 1.3 mu for cotton, same as last year. My son and daughter-in-law work in a factory in Handan, so it’s mostly me and my wife in the fields, with my old mother watching the yard.

For winter wheat, I plant improved seed, the kind the seed station sells every autumn. Last year I got about 480 jin per mu, decent enough. This year I’ll put down 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — that’s 25 kg, the 15-15-15 kind in the green bag. Then at green-up time in March, I’ll spread another 40 jin of urea per mu. That urea is strong stuff, 46% nitrogen, so those 40 jin give me about 9 kg of nitrogen, and the compound gives another 4 kg or so. Total nitrogen around 16 kg per mu. The compound also gives me phosphorus and potassium, about 6 kg each. I irrigate three times: winter water after planting, jointing water when it warms up, and one more at grain filling. The well pump costs electricity, but you can’t skip it. I spray twice — once for weeds, once for bugs. I rotary till before planting wheat.

Summer maize is on the same 6.5 mu, planted right after wheat harvest in early June. I buy hybrid seed from the dealer, about 5 jin per mu. No time to plough deep — I direct-seed into the wheat stubble, maybe a light rotary pass if there’s time. I put compound fertilizer in at planting, about 40 jin per mu, then top dress with urea at the trumpet leaf stage, about 35 jin per mu. That gives me about 15 kg nitrogen per mu, and the compound gives about 5 kg phosphorus and 4 kg potassium. Maize drinks a lot at tasseling, so I irrigate twice. Two pesticide sprays.

For cotton on my 1.3 mu, I plant hybrid Bt cotton in late April. I plough that field in spring because it sat empty all winter. Base fertilizer is 40 jin of compound per mu plus some pig manure from my yard. I top dress twice with urea, about 30 jin total per mu. That gives about 14 kg nitrogen per mu, 5 kg phosphorus, 5 kg potassium. Cotton is fussy — I irrigate three times and spray five times for bollworms, aphids, and mites. If the weather cooperates, I should get about 200 jin of seed cotton per mu.

I watch what Old Wang and the others do. If they add more fertilizer this year, I’ll add a bit too. Fertilizer costs money — urea went up again — but last year the grain price was decent. I’d rather spend a few extra yuan on fertilizer than risk an empty grain head. A bad harvest means borrowing money. Waste some fertilizer? That’s just a cost you absorb. Change what’s been working? That’s risky.
